name: Babelfish for PostgreSQL
tagline: Lets PostgreSQL understand SQL Server's T-SQL and TDS protocol, so SQL Server apps can migrate.
description: Babelfish is an open-source capability, led by AWS, that adds a SQL Server-compatible endpoint to PostgreSQL. It implements the TDS wire protocol plus T-SQL syntax and semantics (procedures, IDENTITY, temp tables, many system views and functions), so applications using SQL Server drivers and tools like SSMS can connect with little or no code change, while the same data stays reachable through normal PostgreSQL. It ships as a set of extensions over a lightly modified PostgreSQL fork, and AWS offers it as a managed option in Aurora PostgreSQL. Coverage is broad but not complete, so the Babelfish Compass tool should be used to assess T-SQL compatibility before migrating.
developer: Amazon Web Services and Babelfish community

pricing.notes: Open source; on AWS it is included in Aurora PostgreSQL pricing at no extra charge.

scale.notes: Inherits PostgreSQL/Aurora scaling: one writer with read replicas.

strengths: SQL Server clients, drivers and SSMS connect via TDS unchanged
Same database accessible through T-SQL and PostgreSQL at once
Babelfish Compass reports compatibility gaps before migration
Managed on Aurora with no extra license fee
weaknesses: Incomplete T-SQL coverage (some system procs, CLR, SQL Agent features missing)
Requires a modified PostgreSQL build, not stock Postgres
Performance characteristics differ from SQL Server, so query tuning is needed
useCases: Migrating SQL Server applications to PostgreSQL
Reducing SQL Server licensing on AWS
Gradual rewrite of T-SQL apps to native PostgreSQL
notIdealFor: Apps relying on SQL Server-only features like CLR integration or SSIS
Workloads needing full SQL Server behavioral parity
